summary: Not a root grown from a verb or noun but a pointing word in its own right, one of the oldest in the Semitic languages: a consonant ḏ (Hebrew ז, Aramaic ד, Arabic ذ) that points at what is before the speaker. זֶה (feminine זֹאת) is "this": with a noun ("this day", Lev 23:14), alone ("this is the thing Yahweh commanded"), "the one … the other", "here", and, after a question, "then" ("who then is the king of glory?"). The same pointer also joins a clause to a noun, "the one who, which": so poetic זוּ ("the people whom you redeemed", Exo 15:13) and scripture's Aramaic דִּי, which is also "of" and "that", and so its counterparts from Arabic to Ge'ez.

words.summary: Masculine זֶה, feminine זֹאת, with no plural of its own ("these" is אֵלֶּה, another word). After a noun with the article it takes the article too (הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, "this day"); alone it stands for a person or thing, and the feminine זֹאת for a matter or deed. Its other uses grow from pointing: at a place ("here"), at a time reached ("now these twenty years"), and, after a question word, at the thing asked about ("why then?"). In a few poems it joins a clause to a noun, as זוּ does.

senses.definition: Follows a noun and points it out as the one present, spoken of, or just named: "this day", "this month", "this place". With the article on both, הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה.

evidence.note: עַד־עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה: "until this very day", the day of the wave-sheaf.
הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים: "this month shall be to you the head of months".
"on the fifteenth day of this month", the month just named.
"on the tenth of this seventh month".
"How fearful is this place!"
לֵךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ לָעָם הַזֶּה: "go and say to this people"; quoted as τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ (Act 28:26).

senses.definition: Stands alone for someone or something present or just spoken of, often as the subject of a clause with no verb: "this is …". The feminine זֹאת stands for a matter, a deed or a word as a whole, where English says "this" or "it".

evidence.note: זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יַהְוֶה: "this is the thing which Yahweh commanded".
זֹאת הַפַּעַם עֶצֶם מֵעֲצָמַי … לְזֹאת יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה: "this one at last is bone of my bones … this one shall be called woman".
מַה־זֹּאת עָשִׂית: "what is this you have done?", the feminine for a deed.
זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם: "this is the book of the generations of Adam".
זֶה יְנַחֲמֵנוּ: "this one will comfort us", of Noah.
זֶה־שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם וְזֶה זִכְרִי לְדֹר דֹּר: "this is my name for ever, and this my memorial to generation after generation".
מֵאֵת יַהְוֶה הָיְתָה זֹּאת: "from Yahweh this came about"; the Greek keeps the feminine, αὕτη (Mat 21:42).
כִּי זֹאת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר אֶכְרֹת: "for this is the covenant that I will cut"; quoted at Heb 8:10.
אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם־בֵּית אֱלֹהִים וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם: "this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven".

senses.definition: Of a person, without his name or with it, the bare "this one" can belittle him.

evidence.note: כִּי־זֶה מֹשֶׁה הָאִישׁ: "as for this Moses, the man who brought us up"; Stephen repeats it, ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος (Act 7:40).
מַה־יֹּשִׁעֵנוּ זֶה: "how will this one save us?", and they despised him.
"how long shall this one be a snare to us?"

senses.definition: Repeated, זֶה … זֶה points first at one and then at another: "this one … that one", and with a preposition, "one to another".

evidence.note: וְלֹא־קָרַב זֶה אֶל־זֶה כָּל־הַלָּיְלָה: "the one did not come near the other all night", the camps of Egypt and Israel.
וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל־זֶה: "and one called to another".
זֹאת אֹמֶרֶת … וְזֹאת אֹמֶרֶת: "this woman says … and that one says".
"and one said thus, and another said thus".
זֶה יַשְׁפִּיל וְזֶה יָרִים: "he brings one low and lifts another up".

senses.definition: Set after מִי, מָה or לָמָּה, it points at the very thing asked about and sharpens the question: "who then?", "why now?".

evidence.note: לָמָּה זֶּה צָחֲקָה שָׂרָה: "why then did Sarah laugh?"
מִי זֶה מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד: "who then is the king of glory?", answered "Yahweh strong and mighty".
מַה־זֶּה מִהַרְתָּ לִמְצֹא: "how is it that you found it so quickly?"
לָמָּה זֶּה אָנֹכִי: "why then am I [thus]?"
מִי־זֶה בָּא מֵאֱדוֹם: "who is this coming from Edom?"
"who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?"

senses.gloss: now (these …), already (with a length of time or a number)
senses.definition: Before a number of years, days or times, it points at the span reached up to now: "these twenty years", "now twice".

evidence.note: זֶה עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ: "these twenty years I have been with you".
וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים: "they have tested me now ten times".
זֶה־לִּי עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה בְּבֵיתֶךָ: "these twenty years I have been in your house".
וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי זֶה פַעֲמַיִם: "he has supplanted me these two times".
"we would have been back twice by now".
כִּי־זֶה שְׁנָתַיִם הָרָעָב: "for these two years the famine has been in the land".
זֶה יָמִים אוֹ־זֶה שָׁנִים: "these days, or these years".

senses.gloss: here; (מִזֶּה) from here, on this side
senses.definition: Pointing at a place: "here", "this way"; with מִן, "from here"; repeated, מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, "on this side and on that"; with בְּ, בָּזֶה, "here".

evidence.note: עֲלוּ זֶה בַּנֶּגֶב: "go up this way into the Negev".
נָסְעוּ מִזֶּה: "they have set out from here".
מִזֶּה אֶחָד וּמִזֶּה אֶחָד: "one on this side and one on that", holding up Moses' hands.
יְשַׁלַּח אֶתְכֶם מִזֶּה: "he will send you out from here".
אַל־תַּעֲלֵנוּ מִזֶּה: "do not bring us up from here".
מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה הֵם כְּתֻבִים: the tablets "written on the one side and on the other".
גָּדֵר מִזֶּה וְגָדֵר מִזֶּה: "a wall on this side and a wall on that".
לֹא־הָיְתָה בָזֶה קְדֵשָׁה: "there has been no cult prostitute here".

senses.definition: With בְּ, the feminine points at the means or sign by which something will be shown, or the terms on which it will be done.

evidence.note: בְּזֹאת תֵּדַע כִּי אֲנִי יַהְוֶה: "by this you shall know that I am Yahweh", the water turned to blood.
בְּזֹאת תִּבָּחֵנוּ: "by this you shall be tested".
בְּזֹאת אֵדַע כִּי כֵנִים אַתֶּם: "by this I shall know that you are honest men".
אַךְ־בְּזֹאת נֵאוֹת לָכֶם: "only on this condition will we consent to you".

senses.gloss: such, the like of this (כָּזֶה, כָּזֹאת)
senses.definition: With כְּ, "as this": one such as this, a thing like this.

evidence.note: הֲנִמְצָא כָזֶה אִישׁ: "can we find a man such as this, in whom is the spirit of God?"
מִי־שָׁמַע כָּזֹאת: "who has heard such a thing as this?"

senses.definition: In a few poems זֶה joins a clause to a noun, as זוּ does: "the place which you founded". The Greek renders it with the relative, ὅν (Psa 104:8).

evidence.note: אֶל־מְקוֹם זֶה יָסַדְתָּ לָהֶם: "to the place which you founded for them".
הַר־צִיּוֹן זֶה שָׁכַנְתָּ בּוֹ: "Mount Zion, in which you have dwelt".
שְׁמַע לְאָבִיךָ זֶה יְלָדֶךָ: "listen to your father who begot you".
וְזֶה־אָהַבְתִּי נֶהְפְּכוּ־בִי: "and those whom I loved have turned against me".

senses.definition: Twice Yahweh is called זֶה סִינַי. Read with the cognates, where the same word before a place or clan names its owner or lord (Arabic ذُو, Sabaic ḏ- before a god's sanctuary), it is a title, "the One of Sinai". Read plainly it is "this Sinai": Sinai itself quaking before Yahweh. Scripture's use alone does not decide between them.

evidence.note: הָרִים נָזְלוּ מִפְּנֵי יַהְוֶה זֶה סִינַי מִפְּנֵי יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: "the mountains quaked before Yahweh, the One of Sinai (or: this Sinai), before Yahweh the God of Israel".
מִפְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים זֶה סִינַי מִפְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: the same words, with אֱלֹהִים.
ταύτῃ for הַזֶּה in "until this very day".
αὕτη for זֹאת: "this is the covenant".
αὕτη for זֹּאת: "from the Lord this came about".
αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι: quoting Jer 31:33; again Heb 10:16.
παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη: quoting Psa 118:23, the feminine kept from זֹאת.
καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρ' ἐμοῦ διαθήκη: from Isa 59:21, וַאֲנִי זֹאת בְּרִיתִי.
ὁ λαὸς οὗτος, quoting Isa 29:13, הָעָם הַזֶּה.
πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον, quoting Isa 6:9.
ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, quoting Exo 32:1.
For מִזֶּה: "they have set out from here".
For מִזֶּה: "do not bring us up from here".
ὅν for relative זֶה: "the place which you founded".
"on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt".

phrases.gloss: this is the thing which Yahweh commanded

evidence.note: "this is the law of the burnt offering".
וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה: "and this is the law".
The son's question at the redemption of the firstborn.
"what is this that God has done to us?"
כִּי מִי הוּא־זֶה עָרַב אֶת־לִבּוֹ: "for who is he that has pledged his heart to approach me?"

phrases.gloss: on this side and on that

evidence.note: "for this let every godly one pray to you".
"for this gird yourselves with sackcloth".

phrases.gloss: this is the day Yahweh has made

words.gloss: this (feminine), a rarer form of זֹאת; (זוֹ) which
words.summary: The feminine without the -t of זֹאת, as Phoenician wrote its feminine z; most of its uses are in Ecclesiastes. Spelled זוֹ it is "this" at Hos 7:16 and the relative "which" at Psa 132:12, as זוּ is.

senses.definition: As זֹאת: this thing, this one.

evidence.note: גַּם־זֹה רָאִיתִי אָנִי כִּי מִיַּד הָאֱלֹהִים הִיא: "this too I saw, that it is from the hand of God".
זֹה הַלִּשְׁכָּה: "this chamber, which faces south".
וְלֹא זֹה הָעִיר: "and this is not the city", beside לֹא זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ.
וּלְשִׂמְחָה מַה־זֹּה עֹשָׂה: "and of mirth, what does this do?"
זוֹ לַעְגָּם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם: "this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt".

senses.definition: With כְּ, feminine and masculine together: "so and so", standing for words or deeds not repeated.

evidence.note: כָּזֹה וְכָזֶה עָשָׂה לִי מִיכָה: "thus and thus Micah has done for me".
"the sword devours one as well as another".
כָּזֹה וְכָזֶה תְּדַבֵּר אֵלֶיהָ: "thus and thus shall you speak to her".

senses.definition: Once joining a clause to a noun, as זוּ.

evidence.note: וְעֵדֹתִי זוֹ אֲלַמְּדֵם: "and my testimony which I shall teach them".

words.summary: The pointing word as a relative, never changing for gender or number: it follows the noun and introduces the clause that says which one. It belongs to the songs and Psalms (Exo 15, Isa 42–43, the Psalms, Hab 1:11), as the indeclinable ذُو of the Arabs of Ṭayyiʾ, Ugaritic d and Aramaic דִּי do the same work.

senses.definition: Joins a clause to the noun before it: "the people whom you redeemed", "the net which they hid", "the way in which I should walk".

evidence.note: נָחִיתָ בְחַסְדְּךָ עַם־זוּ גָּאָלְתָּ: "in your kindness you led the people whom you redeemed"; the Greek has ὅν.
בְּרֶשֶׁת־זוּ טָמָנוּ נִלְכְּדָה רַגְלָם: "in the net which they hid their own foot is caught".
עַד־יַעֲבֹר עַם־זוּ קָנִיתָ: "until the people pass over whom you have purchased".
עַם־זוּ יָצַרְתִּי לִי: "the people whom I formed for myself".
הֲלוֹא יַהְוֶה זוּ חָטָאנוּ לוֹ: "was it not Yahweh, against whom we have sinned?"
בִּמְזִמּוֹת זוּ חָשָׁבוּ: "in the schemes which they have devised".
בְּדֶרֶךְ־זוּ תֵלֵךְ: "in the way in which you shall go".
הוֹדִיעֵנִי דֶּרֶךְ־זוּ אֵלֵךְ: "make me know the way in which I should walk".
שְׁתַּיִם־זוּ שָׁמָעְתִּי: "twice, this I have heard", or "two things which I have heard".
זוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ: "what you have wrought for us".
מִן־הַדּוֹר זוּ לְעוֹלָם: "from this generation for ever", the pointing sense still near.
זוּ כֹחוֹ לֵאלֹהוֹ: "he whose strength is his god".
ὅν for זוּ: "the people whom you redeemed".
ᾧ for זוּ: "against whom we sinned".

words.summary: The article and a pointing לָ before ז: the one over there, or the one in view. The same build as Arabic اَلَّذِى (al-la-ḏī), which in Arabic has become the relative "who". It and its longer forms הַלָּזֶה and הַלֵּזוּ are kept as words of their own, as the text spells them.

senses.definition: Points out a person or thing in sight, often at some distance: "that rock", "that Shunammite", "that monument".

evidence.note: הִנֵּה הַשׁוּנַּמִּית הַלָּז: "look, there is that Shunammite", seen from far off (מִנֶּגֶד).
מָה הַצִּיּוּן הַלָּז אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי רֹאֶה: "what is that monument that I see?"
אֲשֶׁר מֵעֵבֶר הַלָּז: "which is on the other side, yonder".
אֶל־הַסֶּלַע הַלָּז: "on this rock".
הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַלָּז beside הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הֶעָרֵל הַזֶּה in the same verse: "this Philistine".
אֶל־הַנַּעַר הַלָּז: "to that young man".
הָבֵן לְהַלָּז אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶה: "make this man understand the vision".

parallels.note: "this Philistine" is first הַלָּז, then הַזֶּה, in one breath.

senses.definition: Of a man seen approaching, sometimes with scorn.

evidence.note: מִי־הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה הַהֹלֵךְ בַּשָּׂדֶה לִקְרָאתֵנוּ: "who is that man walking in the field to meet us?"
הִנֵּה בַּעַל הַחֲלֹמוֹת הַלָּזֶה בָּא: "look, this master of dreams is coming".

senses.definition: Points at the land just spoken of.

evidence.note: הָאָרֶץ הַלֵּזוּ הַנְּשַׁמָּה הָיְתָה כְּגַן־עֵדֶן: "this land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden".

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic for זֶה: ד for the older ḏ, with the -n that Sabaic ḏn and Byblian zn also add. Masculine, and alone a matter: "this".

senses.definition: Follows a noun and points it out.

evidence.note: עַל־רָזָה דְּנָה: "concerning this secret".
לְמִגְלֵא רָזָה דְנָה: "to reveal this secret".
כְּתָבָה דְנָה: "this writing".

senses.definition: Stands alone for what has just been told, or as the subject of a clause with no verb.

evidence.note: חֶלְמָךְ וְחֶזְוֵי רֵאשָׁךְ … דְּנָה הוּא: "your dream and the visions of your head … are this".
עַל־דְּנָה פִּתְגָם: "concerning this matter".
"for this reason this city was laid waste".
כִּדְנָה תֵּאמְרוּן לְהוֹם: "thus shall you say to them".

words.summary: The feminine of the Aramaic pointing word, with the same vowel as Arabic ذَا.

senses.definition: Points at a city or a horn.

evidence.note: הֲלָא דָא־הִיא בָּבֶל רַבְּתָא: "is not this great Babylon?"
בְּקַרְנָא־דָא: "in this horn".

senses.definition: Repeated, as זֶה … זֶה: "one against another", "one from another".

evidence.note: וְאַרְכֻבָּתֵהּ דָּא לְדָא נָקְשָׁן: "and his knees knocked one against the other".
שָׁנְיָן דָּא מִן־דָּא: "different one from another".

words.summary: The pointing word with -k, which points further off, as in Arabic ذَاكَ, ذٰلِكَ "that". In Ezra's letters and decrees.

senses.definition: Points out a city, a house or a man already spoken of.

evidence.note: דִּי הֵן קִרְיְתָא דָךְ תִּתְבְּנֵא: "that if this city is built".
קִרְיְתָא דָךְ קִרְיָא מָרָדָא: "that city is a rebellious city".
שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר דֵּךְ: "that Sheshbazzar".
בֵּית־אֱלָהָא דֵךְ: "this house of God", twice.

words.summary: דֵּךְ with -n added. Only in Daniel's visions, of the image and of the little horn.

senses.definition: Points at something seen in a vision.

evidence.note: צַלְמָא דִכֵּן רַב: "that image was great".
וְקַרְנָא דִכֵּן וְעַיְנִין לַהּ: "and that horn which had eyes".
וְקַרְנָא דִכֵּן עָבְדָה קְרָב עִם־קַדִּישִׁין: "that horn made war with the holy ones".

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic counterpart of זוּ, and far commoner: it does the work of אֲשֶׁר, of the construct state, and of כִּי. With prepositions it makes conjunctions: כָּל־קֳבֵל דִּי "because", עַד דִּי "until", מָה דִּי "what".

senses.definition: Joins a clause to the noun before it, or with no noun before it, "the one who".

evidence.note: אֱלָהִין דִּי מְדָרְהוֹן עִם־בִּשְׂרָא לָא אִיתוֹהִי: "gods whose dwelling is not with flesh".
שָׁלְטָנֵהּ שָׁלְטָן עָלַם דִּי־לָא יֶעְדֵּה: "his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away".
בָּבֶל רַבְּתָא דִּי־אֲנָה בֱנַיְתַהּ: "great Babylon, which I have built".
וּלְמַן־דִּי יִצְבֵּא יִתְּנִנַּהּ: "and gives it to whomever he will".

senses.definition: Between two nouns, "the one of": the name of God, the servants of the God of heaven; with a pronoun, "his".

evidence.note: שְׁמֵהּ דִּי־אֱלָהָא: "the name of God"; and דִּי חָכְמְתָא וּגְבוּרְתָא דִּי לֵהּ־הִיא, "wisdom and might are his".
עַבְדוֹהִי דִי־אֱלָהּ שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְעָא: "the servants of the God of heaven and earth".
אֱלָהַיָּא דִּי־שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְקָא לָא עֲבַדוּ: "the gods who did not make the heavens and the earth".
אֱלָהֵהּ דִּי־דָנִיֵּאל: "the God of Daniel".

senses.definition: After a verb of knowing, saying or decreeing, introduces what is known or said.

evidence.note: מִן־יַצִּיב יָדַע אֲנָה דִּי עִדָּנָא אַנְתּוּן זָבְנִין: "I know for certain that you are gaining time".
עַד־דִּבְרַת דִּי יִנְדְּעוּן חַיַּיָּא דִּי־שַׁלִּיט עִלָּאָה: "to the end that the living may know that the Most High rules".
שִׂים טְעֵם דִּי: "a decree is made, that …".

senses.definition: Gives the reason; with כָּל־קֳבֵל, "because of the fact that".

evidence.note: דִּי יְכֵלְתָּ לְמִגְלֵא רָזָה דְנָה: "since you have been able to reveal this secret".
דִּי חָכְמְתָא וּגְבוּרְתָא יְהַבְתְּ לִי: "for you have given me wisdom and might".
כָּל־קֳבֵל דִּי־הֲוָא עָבֵד: "as he had been doing".

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܕ, דִּי shortened to a prefix, written on the word it governs.

senses.definition: Joins a clause to a noun, marks the owner after a noun, and introduces what is said or known: all the work of Biblical Aramaic דִּי.

evidence.note: יֵשֻוע דּמֵתקרֵא משִיחָא: "Jesus who is called Messiah".
אֵמרֵה דַּאלָהָא הַו דּשָקֵל חטִיתֵה דּעָלמָא: "the lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world".
יִדַען דּהָנַו שַרִירָאיִת משִיחָא: "we know that this is truly the Messiah".

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܗܳܕܶܐ, "lo, this", built as Arabic هٰذَا. The masculine ܗܳܢܳܐ is from another pointing word.

senses.definition: Where the Hebrew has זֹאת, the Peshitta's quotation keeps the feminine.

evidence.note: מֵן לוָת מָריָא הוָת הָדֵא: "from the Lord this came about", Psa 118:23's זֹּאת.
הָדֵא דֵּין דִּיַתִקִא: "this is the covenant", Jer 31:33's זֹאת הַבְּרִית.

cognates.gloss: this (masculine); feminine ذِى, ذِهْ; with هَا, هٰذَا "this"
cognates.note: The same pointing word, "properly meaning This", with ḏ where Hebrew has ז and Aramaic ד. Lane's sources also say "the noun in it is ذَ", the consonant alone, the vowels being endings. Arabic adds -k for the far one (ذَاكَ, ذٰلِكَ), as Aramaic דֵּךְ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 947, art. ذا, ذَا
evidence.note: "a noun of indication, [properly meaning This …]"; fem. ذِى and ذِهْ.
"this"; compares Ge'ez ዝ and Hebrew זה.

cognates.gloss: possessor of, he of; (dialect of Ṭayyiʾ) who, which, indeclinable
cognates.note: The pointing word as "the one of": ذُو مَالٍ "one of wealth", and in names and titles, ذُو يَزَنَ, ذُو الخَلَصَةِ (a sanctuary). In the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ it is the relative "who, which", unchanged for gender and number, as Hebrew זוּ is.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 984, art. ذو, ذُو
evidence.note: "A possessor, an owner"; § b16: "used in the sense of اَلَّذِى, in the dial. of Teiyi … it retains the same form when it denotes a dual and a pl. and a fem."

cognates.note: Article, a pointing لَ and ذِى: the same build as Hebrew הַלָּזֶה, though in Arabic it has become the relative.

evidence.note: "formed from اَل (al-, the) + لَ (la) + ذِي (ḏī, this). Compare Biblical Hebrew הלזה".

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 984, art. ذو, § b16
evidence.note: ذُو "used in the sense of اَلَّذِى".

cognates.gloss: that of, which (determinative and relative pronoun); also a conjunction
cognates.note: Inflected for gender and number (m. d, f. dt, as Hebrew זֹאת has -t); the older texts write it with ḏ, Standard Ugaritic with d.

evidence.note: "that of/which"; "Like the Arabic cognate, the older Ugaritic form is ḏ (1.24:45), but Standard Ugaritic uses forms in d"; § 57.3: "can also be used as a conjunction".
"the relative pronoun".

cognates.note: Tyro-Sidonian Phoenician and Punic, following its noun without the article, as in "this coffin", "this gate". Byblian has zn "that" beside z "this", with the -n of Aramaic דְּנָה.

evidence.note: "[Heb. ze, fem. zo] … pron. 1. THIS"; KAI 14.3–4 bḥlt z wbqbr z, "in this coffin and in this tomb".
Byblian z "this here" against zn "this there, that, yonder".

cognates.note: The same letter as the relative in the oldest Byblian inscriptions: "the coffin which Ittobaal made".

evidence.note: "[Heb. zu, ze; Ug. d-] pr. WHICH, THAT (archaic, proclitic relative pronoun; found in Old Byblian inscriptions only)"; KAI 1.1 ʾrn zpʿl, "the coffin that … made".

cognates.gloss: who, which; he of, that of (relative pronoun, masculine singular)
cognates.note: Sabaic (Old South Arabian). Both the relative ("booty which satisfied him") and "he of": a man of a clan, a god of his sanctuary, a statue of gold.

evidence.note: "relative pn, m.s. … (HE) WHO, (THAT) WHICH"; "in epithets of gods: '(the god) A. of (the sanctuary) D.'"; compares Arabic ḏū.

cognates.note: Sabaic: the pointing ḏ- with -n, as Aramaic דְּנָה and Byblian zn: ḏn ṣlmn "this statue".

evidence.note: "demonstrative adj, m.s.: THIS [Cf Ar deictic element ḏū-, ḏā- and Sab ḏ- (relative pn, m.s); here extended by the 'nominalizing' suffix -n.]"

cognates.note: Alone and before a noun; also the longer ዝንቱ. Ge'ez z stands for both older z and ḏ, so it does not show which.

evidence.note: "pron. demonstr. m. … hic, haec, hoc".

cognates.gloss: who, which (relative pronoun); of (mark of the genitive)
cognates.note: Relative and genitive in one, as Aramaic דִּי: ኢየሱስ ዘተብህለ ክርስቶስ, "Jesus who is called Christ" (Mat 1:16).

evidence.note: "pron. rel. et conj. rel. … qui, quae, quod"; followed by ዘ "nota Genitivi".

cognates.gloss: who, which, where; of (with pronouns, דִּילִי "mine")
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the same particle as Biblical Aramaic דִּי, mostly as a prefix דְּ־.

evidence.note: "who, which, where, whom &c. Dan. IV, 5 … Mostly as prefix: דִּי־, דִּ־, דְּ־"; with pronouns דִּידִי, דִּילִי "mine".
"who, which, that, what"; "From דִּי, ultimately from Proto-Semitic *ḏV- ('this')".

cognates.translit: dēn, dənā; fem. dā; far deixis dēk
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, the same forms as scripture's דְּנָה, דָּא and דֵּךְ, with הָדֵין "this" built as Arabic هٰذَا.

evidence.note: "(cmp. דָּא, דֵּךְ) this, that"; הָדֵן "= הָא ד׳"; מן קדמת דנא "ere this, formerly".
"(דא with formative ך) this, that. Ezra V, 16".

doctrine.statement: "The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; from Yahweh this (זֹּאת) came about … This (זֶה) is the day Yahweh has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it" (Psa 118:22–24): each "this" points back to the rejected stone made head. Jesus applies the verses to himself (Mat 21:42), and Peter says the stone is Jesus, "whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead" (Act 4:10–11). From the verses: the day Yahweh made, in which the psalm rejoices, is the day the rejected one was raised and exalted.

"This (זֶה) is my name for ever", Yahweh says of his own name (Exo 3:15). Of the righteous branch raised to David it is said, "this (זֶה) is his name by which he will be called: Yahweh our righteousness" (Jer 23:5–6); and of Jerusalem in the same words, "this (זֶה) is what she will be called: Yahweh our righteousness" (Jer 33:16). From the verses: to be called by this name is to bear Yahweh's name, declaring what Yahweh is to his people; the city bears it as the king does, so the name names what Yahweh has done in them and does not make either of them Yahweh himself.

note: Root question: no verbal or nominal root was found. The word is the Semitic pointing (deictic) element *ḏ-, with vowel endings for gender and case (Arabic ḏā, ḏī, ḏū; Ugaritic d/ḏ, f. dt; Sabaic ḏ-, ḏn; Ge'ez zə, za; Aramaic dā, dī, dənā; Phoenician z, zn), found in every branch; scripture has no noun or verb זהה/זוה/זיה from which it could have grown, and Arabic grammarians' reconstructions of ذَا as ذَوَى or ذَيَى (Lane p. 947) only fit it to the root pattern. The later Hebrew verb זִהָה "identify" is formed from זֶה, not the reverse. So the entry is keyed by its own consonants, זה, and the evidence for the pointing word itself is as strong as for any Semitic word. One pointer serves as demonstrative and relative across the languages (Hebrew זוּ and poetic זֶה, Aramaic דִּי, Ugaritic d, Sabaic ḏ-, Ge'ez za, Old Byblian z, Arabic ḏū in Ṭayyiʾ), which is why the relative words are kept here. Not this element: Hebrew שֶׁ־ and Akkadian ša (Akkadian keeps ḏ as z, so ša does not answer to ḏ; Wiktionary's comparison of ša with ذَا is not followed); אֵלֶּה "these" and Aramaic אִלֵּין (another pointing word, ʾl); Syriac ܗܳܢܳܐ "this" (hn); the month name זִו (זיו "brightness"). BDB files זֹאת under זֶה (g.ah.aa); its cross-reference key g.ab.ad has no tokens and is claimed here. g.ai.aa and g.aj.aa list the same two tokens of זוֹ (Hos 7:16, Psa 132:12); both keys are on זֹה, so they are counted twice there. Zec 2:8 and Psa 68:9 are cited by the Hebrew numbering (English 2:4, 68:8); Dan 4:14, 4:22, 4:27, 4:29 and 6:11 likewise (English 4:17, 4:25, 4:30, 4:32, 6:10). Not consulted: CAL (refuses automated access), DULAT, Leslau, Old Aramaic inscriptions (znh, zy). Dillmann's column numbers were read from the Internet Archive OCR and should be checked on the page image. זֶה סִינַי is left open between a title ("the One of Sinai") and "this Sinai". The particle's senses are illustrative, not exhaustive: about 1,800 tokens.
